There is no CEO-only workspace, so CEO actions and F&B-manager work are mixed. A head-office module id must be placed in a workspace in the same change.

gaps:
1. No head office record. Nothing lets the CEO create several head offices or choose which companies sit under each.
2. No single place where head office staff are employed and paid. Today they are employees of whichever company (GS Foods) and count in that company's HR and headcount. If one person works for two companies they need two employee records (decision 31).
3. No posting of shared cost to the books:
   - TenantContribution and Position cost-share are planning numbers only.
   - There are no intercompany accounts (due to / due from head office, recharge income/expense).
   - The allocation engine cannot cross companies.
   So every company's real P&L shows either all of the head office cost (GS Foods) or none of it.
4. Visibility for head office staff is manual: a TenantMember row per user per company, kept in sync by hand. Adding a company under a head office would not give that head office's staff access to it. TenantMember also grants WRITE in every member company. That is broader than 'see across my companies' and needs deciding.
5. The reporting line stops at the company boundary (/hr/team uses me.tenantId only). An HO HOD cannot be the manager or approver of outlet staff in another company.
6. Approvals cannot be reassigned:
   - Every CEO queue is gated by role (admin, or admin/owner).
   - The queues are spread over /workforce, /procurement, /accounting/recipes/approvals, the /storefront Approvals tab, payroll and /hr/approvals.
   - There is no single CEO inbox and no 'assign this queue to <HO person>'.
   - The CLAUDE.md rule says 'Nothing publishes without the CEO (role admin)' for the storefront, so delegating that changes a documented rule.
7. The name 'head office' is already used for the within-company 'Head office (unallocated)' P&L line. That will confuse people once real head offices exist.
8. No CEO-only workspace. CEO actions (companies, logins, module access, approvals, head offices) sit in Operations next to F&B-manager work, so the owner cannot hand Operations to an F&B manager.
9. No company-separation tests exist for a three-level case: head office, company A, and a company that is not under it.

options.option: A. Head office = a Tenant of kind 'head_office', plus a HeadOfficeCompany link table, plus a monthly recharge run (extend the allocation engine to company-level targets) with intercompany journal entries
options.pros:
Reuses the most existing structure with one source of truth:
- HO staff are ordinary HrEmployees of the HO tenant, paid by the existing HR payroll and posted by hr/ledger.ts to the HO's own books. No change to payroll code, and one employee record per person.
- Books stay per company by construction. The recharge posts Dr 'Head office charges' / Cr 'Due to head office' in each company and Dr 'Due from <company>' / Cr 'Head office recharges' in the HO, each with its own tenantId, through postJournalEntry.
- Supports multiple head offices, and the CEO picks companies by editing the link table.
- HO staff visibility can be worked out from the link table in the auth middleware (memberTenantIds ∪ companies under the user's HOs, read-only by default), so no TenantMember copies need syncing.
- Replaces TenantContribution(head_office), Department.isHeadOffice and the free-text costShareNote rather than adding a second mechanism. labour-budget nets against the recharge instead.
options.cons:
- An HO tenant must be kept out of everything a trading company has (brands, orders, storefront, the company switcher's 'trading' lists, /health revenue checks), so every tenant list needs a `kind` filter.
- New chart codes need the CA's choice of names.
- Reading access across companies is a new crossing of company separation, like FleetAgreement. It needs its own two-company and HO tests.
- Existing HO people employed in GS Foods must be moved to the HO tenant (new employee records, payroll cut-over month).

options.option: B. A head office without its own books: a HeadOffice model (name, payingTenantId) + HeadOfficeCompany links. HO staff stay employees of the paying company, and a recharge run moves the shared cost from the paying company to the others
options.pros:
- Matches today's reality exactly (GS Foods issues the salaries) and needs no new tenant, so no tenant list filtering.
- Still supports several head offices with CEO-chosen companies.
- The recharge still gives correct per-company P&Ls.
- Smaller migration: nobody changes employer.
options.cons:
- The head office is not a separate unit. Its staff, HR records, payroll and headcount sit inside the paying company, which that company's HR and finance can see and the other companies cannot.
- An HOD's reports in other companies still need a cross-company reporting line.
- When a second company should pay instead, the people have to move anyway.
- The paying company's P&L shows the gross cost minus the recharge, which is harder to read.

options.option: C. Minimal: keep TenantContribution, add a 'head office group' label to it, and have active head_office contributions post a monthly intercompany journal entry
options.pros:
- Smallest change.
- Reuses the existing contributions UI, the netting in labour-budget/opex/projections, and the 'operator belongs to both companies' guard.
- Puts the shared cost in the books.
options.cons:
- No real head office, so 'make multiple head offices and pick companies' becomes a pile of pairwise contribution rows.
- No salary-drawing layer: HO staff stay inside one company.
- Does not solve visibility, cross-company HODs or approvals.
- Fixed amounts only (no % or revenue driver) unless the allocation logic is copied, and copying it would create the duplicate the standing rule forbids.

options.option: D. Add-on to A or B, separate piece: approval routing. One ApprovalAssignment table (scope = head office or company, queue = logins | purchase_orders | recipes | payroll | storefront_publish | hr:<section>, assigneeUserId). One canApprove(req, queue, tenantId) helper replaces the role guards on the existing approve endpoints, and one CEO 'Approvals' inbox page reads all queues
options.pros:
- Answers 'where is my CEO approval thing' and 'reassign approvals to HO people (HODs)'.
- No queue is rebuilt. Each module keeps its own approve endpoint and state, and only the 'who may decide' check and the inbox are shared.
- Fits a new CEO-only workspace in workspaces.ts.
options.cons:
- Touches auth-critical guards in five or more modules. The orchestrator should do it, with a test for each queue.
- Delegating storefront publishing breaks the written 'nothing publishes without the CEO' rule unless the owner agrees.
- An assignee must be blocked from approving their own submissions (canActOnStep already does this for HR).

recommendation:
Option A, done in stages, with D shipped alongside it as a separate piece.

1. Schema:
   - Add `Tenant.kind` ('company' | 'head_office', default 'company').
   - Add `HeadOfficeCompany { headOfficeTenantId, companyTenantId, driver: fixed_pct | revenue_share | fixed_amount, weightBps?, monthlyCents?, startedAt, endedAt }`, with @@unique([headOfficeTenantId, companyTenantId]).
   - Whether one company may sit under two head offices is an owner question.
   - It is a CEO-only route (role admin) with a two-company + HO test.

2. Access: in `attachStaffPrincipal`, add the companies under the head offices the user belongs to as a READ set, worked out from HeadOfficeCompany and never stored as TenantMember copies. Write and approve rights in those companies still come from TenantMember or the D assignments. Removing a company from a head office removes access on the next request.

3. Books:
   - Add a small set of codes to `lib/chartOfAccounts.ts`: a due-from-related-companies asset, a due-to-head-office liability, a head-office charges expense, and a recharge income or contra-expense for the head office. The CA should name them.
   - Extend the allocation engine to company-level targets (a `targetTenantId` per weight, posting one balanced entry per company plus the head office's mirror entry). Do not write a new engine.
   - The run reads the head office's wage and overhead accounts for the month.

4. Remove the duplicates in the same piece of work:
   - TenantContribution(head_office) becomes the HeadOfficeCompany split. Migrate the JV 500k row, and keep the table for commissary/other or retire it if the owner agrees.
   - Department.isHeadOffice and Position.costShareNote for HO seats are superseded, because HO seats live in the HO tenant.
   - labour-budget, opex and projections read the recharge.
   - Rename the brand P&L line 'Head office (unallocated)' to 'Company overhead (unallocated)'.

5. HR: HO HODs are HrEmployees of the HO tenant. Allow `managerId` to point to an employee of a head office that the employee's company sits under. /hr/team and the 'hod' approval step then follow that link across companies.

6. Separately: add a CEO workspace to workspaces.ts (head offices, companies, logins, module access, the approvals inbox, ceo_overview). Operations goes to fnb_manager/management, as the owner asked.

FleetAgreement stays as it is (an operational permission). Its future cost split can later reuse the same recharge run.
questionsForOwner: Is each head office its own company on paper, with its own bank account that pays the HOD salaries? Or does one of your companies (GS Foods today) actually pay them and get paid back by the others?
How should a head office's cost be shared between its companies: a fixed % you set for each company, by each company's sales that month, or a fixed monthly amount (like the JV's 500k today)?

Should the head office charge go into each company's books every month automatically (so each company's P&L shows its share), or stay as a planning number like today? If it goes into the books, can your CA give the names for the 'due to / due from head office' accounts?
Can one company sit under more than one head office (for example the JV under both a GS and a Viva head office), or exactly one?
In the companies under their head office, should HO staff (HODs) only see things, or also edit and approve? Their module access would still limit them either way.
Can outlet staff in a company report to an HOD in the head office (for leave, overtime and other HR approvals), or does each company keep its own managers and the HOD only oversees?
We already have a 'JV contributes 500k to head office' record under Workforce → Positions. OK to replace it with the new head office split and remove the old screen, so there is only one?

Which approvals may you hand to an HOD: new logins, purchase orders, recipes, payroll, HR requests, and storefront publishing? Today the rule is 'nothing publishes on the storefront without the CEO'. Should that change?

To split your CEO hat from your F&B manager hat: OK to make a separate 'CEO' workspace (companies, head offices, logins, module access, all approvals) and give Operations to the F&B manager role, which your login holds too for now?
